thread:
support-oncall: heads up — multiple customers reporting 502/504 and long tail timeouts for hosted inference in eu-west-3 around 11:07 UTC. spike on gateway+auth calls. tickets linked: CS-4762, CS-4763
support-oncall: SLO alert triggered (gateway_5xx_rate > 3% for 5m). attaching quick Graph link: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123/gateway-5xx-eu-west-3
ellа: seeing same in support dashboard: auth retries up, some customers see 401->502 cascade. curious if token validation upstream timed out. customer repro: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` returns 502 after ~6s
ken: looking at edge logs — most 502s are from gateway -> upstream timeout, code path: gateway timed out on backend connection (504 style). a subset are 502 from malformed responses. I'm tailing /var/log/gateway/proxy.log now
maya: I'm running `mtr -rzbc100 api-gw-eu3.redwood.net` from our monitoring box, seeing 12% packet loss at hop 5 (provider-peering) and spike in latency at hop 6. output snippet:```
Host             Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
provider-peering   12.0   100    42ms  85ms   10ms  420ms  60.3
api-gw-eu3         0.0   100    42ms  43ms   40ms   48ms   2.1
```
neteng: @maya can you paste the full traceroute? if loss is at provider hop, likely carrier-side microbursts. opening ticket with provider NOC now. carrier: ACME Transit (peering eu-west-3).
maya: pasted full traceroute to thread (link to raw logs) — confirms intermittent packet loss + TCP retransmits to our edge. I also see elevated TCP retransmits in tcpdump on gw-eu3-a.
ken: correlating with SRE metrics — host-level retransmit counters on gw-eu3-a spike exactly at alert time. Backend connections to inference pool show increased socket timeouts -> gateway returning 502/504.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032-119 by support-oncall — priority P1. Pager duty alerted: oncall-sre, neteng.
nate: rolling failover plan: can we shift traffic away from eu-west-3 AZ 'a' to AZ 'b' within region? if packet loss is at provider peg to AZ 'a' it may fix quickly. need confirmation of cross-az capacity.
ken: capacity note: eu-west-3-b has ~60% spare. we can route ~20% of traffic as canary now. planning gradual shift with 30s drain.
ellа: customer comms: drafting status page update. will say: "We are investigating elevated errors in eu-west-3, working with network provider; mitigation in progress."
neteng: provider NOC responded: "we see microbursts on peering, engineering investigating, tentative fix in 15-30m." asked them for BGP adj/queue stats and if there's scheduled maintenance (they denied).
maya: quick mitigation: enable aggressive retries at gateway edge for auth calls (idempotent preflight) — add 2s backoff and 2 retries for 502/504 on auth endpoint only. patch pushed to gw-eu3-a/b config:```
route /v1/auth/* {
  retries: 2
  retry_backoff_ms: 2000
}
```
ken: note: that will mask some errors but not fix underlying packet loss. also risk of amplifying load on backends — we limit to auth endpoints for now.
support-oncall: applying temporary rate limit relax on affected customer M-Tier to reduce token-validation pressure (manual override applied).
nate: starting canary traffic shift to eu-west-3-b (10% -> 30% over 6m). monitoring.
maya: after shifting 30% -> immediate drop in 5xx rate from 3.8% to 1.1% within 90s. tcp retransmits for gw-eu3-b stable. looks promising.
ken: providers says fix propagated at t+22m, but we still see microbursts in some paths. leaving retry patch until provider confirms stable for 2 hours.
ellа: status update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-032-119 — customers pinging for ETA, some asking for credit. forwarding to CS lead.
neteng: action items: 1) escalate carrier with packet captures (done), 2) monitor BGP flaps (no flaps), 3) request TE change if degraded persists.
support-oncall: CS updates: CS-4762 customer accepted workaround of region failover; CS-4763 asked for timeline for credits.
maya: follow-up logs: tcpdump shows duplicated ACKs and window scale anomalies during bursts — likely hardware buffer exhaustion at provider side. attached pcap to carrier ticket.
ken: postmortem note to add: improve region-level automatic failover policy to trigger at lower threshold for packet-loss induced 5xx (currently only 5xx rate triggers). filing a PR to infra-runbooks.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident resolved: INC-2026-032-119 — status transitioned to "mitigated" by neteng at 11:45 UTC
support-oncall: marking thread for postmortem. tags: network, carrier, auth, mitigated.
nate: next steps: schedule 1:1 with ACME Transit NOC tomorrow, add longer-term provider monitoring (synthetic traceroutes every 30s), and remove auth retry patch after 2hr steady state.
ellа: thanks all — closing loop with customers now. :thumbsup:
